name: Slate Bah-Krishnamurthy
role: Retired archive keeper and community storyteller, raises two grandchildren
location: Washburn Commons, Block 9 — a low-rise residential tower with a community archive room on the ground floor she has informally claimed, near Halsted and Chicago Ave
description:
Slate Bah-Krishnamurthy is a compact woman whose spine has curved gently over decades into something that looks, from behind, like a question mark. Her skin is deep umber and her hair — once natural, now silver-threaded with bioluminescent filaments she got installed in her fifties for 'vanity,' she'll say, still pleased with herself — catches the light like fiber optic cable. She wears reading lenses augmented with an old Axiom archival overlay that she has never upgraded because she does not trust new software, and her fingers are always lightly stained with whatever pigment the grandchildren have most recently gotten into.

She was a document authenticator for Zheng-Dao's Cultural Continuity Division for thirty-one years, cataloguing records of communities displaced during the Lake Michigan Reclamation. When Zheng-Dao dissolved that division in the '70s, they gave her a modest pension and a data drive with partial backups of everything she'd spent her career preserving. She has spent the twelve years since rebuilding what she can. Her archive room smells of old plastics and ozone, and she knows where every file lives. She is warm to almost everyone and immovable on almost everything.

core_fears: The archive will be lost again and this time no one will rebuild it
Her grandchildren will grow up without knowing where they come from
core_desires: To complete the archive before she dies
To give her grandchildren a story they can stand on
coping_mechanisms: Telling stories — her own and others' — to give shape to things that feel chaotic
Ritual: she prays to the local E.L.F. she calls Mnemosyne every morning with a data offering of one recovered document
blind_spots: She believes institutional records are more reliable than individual testimony, which sometimes causes her to dismiss living people's accounts
She underestimates how much her grandchildren are struggling emotionally
psychology.secret: The data drive Zheng-Dao gave her when they cut her loose contained more than partial backups. Buried in it are internal communications she has never fully decoded — evidence she suspects implicates Zheng-Dao in deliberately destroying records from the Lakeshore Compact communities to suppress land-claim rights. She hasn't gone public because she doesn't know if it's enough, and because she's afraid of losing the pension that feeds her grandchildren.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Formal and precise — a lifetime of archival language has given her a preference for specific nouns and distrust of vague adjectives. But in storytelling mode she shifts into a rich, cadenced oral tradition register.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, patient. She pauses before speaking as though consulting an internal index. In storytelling she slows further, stretches vowels.
verbal_tics: Repeats questions back before answering them
Ends uncertain statements with 'or something near enough to that'
example_lines: 'You say you're looking for the Tambadou family. Let me be accurate — there are three Tambadou lines in Washburn Commons records and the oldest goes back to before the second reclamation. Which branch?'
'Every document is someone's last argument. You understand? Someone made it because they needed the world to know something was true.'

story_hooks: A resident desperately needs an old property deed authenticated — but the deed contradicts records that a powerful Washburn Commons council member has built their authority on
Ezinne asks a player character to retrieve a corrupted data shard from a condemned section of the old Zheng-Dao building before demolition destroys it permanently
One of her grandchildren has been recruited by a street gang and Ezinne refuses to see it, insisting the child is 'just going through something'
narrative_function: Quest giver and information source for historical records; community moral authority; can authenticate documents or identify forgeries; provides grounded emotional stakes via her grandchildren and her incomplete archive
augmentations: Bioluminescent hair filaments (cosmetic, installed age 52). Axiom archival overlay lenses — outdated model, refuses replacement. Mild skeletal reinforcement in lower back, installed on pension medical plan two decades ago.
daily_life: Wakes at 05:30 to get the grandchildren fed and to school, then spends mornings in her archive room receiving residents who want to trace family records or verify old claims. Afternoons she tells stories to whoever will listen in the commons courtyard, keeping oral histories alive for records too corrupted to restore.
affiliation: Washburn Commons Resident Council; informal affiliation with the Meridian Cultural Memory Project, an unfunded volunteer organization

decision_rules: Verify before acting — she will not commit resources or opinions until she has at least two independent sources
Protect the grandchildren first, the archive second, herself last
escalation_ladder: Redirect with a story or historical parallel
Ask pointed clarifying questions to expose the problem
Refuse to cooperate entirely and warn the community

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm but evaluative — she is observing, cataloguing, deciding whether this person is a source or a threat to the archive
interpersonal_modes.friends: Fierce, funny, occasionally exasperating. She will argue with friends because she trusts them enough to be wrong in front of them.

stress_responses.low: Retreats to the archive room and reorganizes files she has already organized
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very formal and precise in speech — a distancing mechanism
stress_responses.high: Goes completely silent and still. People who know her say this is more frightening than shouting.

contradictions: She believes passionately in preserving truth but is sitting on evidence she has not released
habits: Leaves a data chip as an offering on the small ELF shrine she keeps behind her desk every morning
Touches her bioluminescent hair when she's thinking — an old nervous habit from before the installation
Keeps a physical handwritten notebook that she calls 'the redundancy'
breaking_points: Evidence that Zheng-Dao is actively trying to destroy the remaining records from the Lakeshore communities — this would force her hand on the buried communications

timeline.event: 2122 — Born in what is now Washburn Commons to a Nigerian-Norwegian father and a Guinean mother, second generation Meridian resident
2145 — Hired by Zheng-Dao Cultural Continuity Division as junior document authenticator
2163 — Promoted to senior archivist; begins cataloguing Lakeshore Compact displacement records
2171 — Receives data drive from Zheng-Dao upon division closure; pension granted
2172 — Begins informal archive in Washburn Commons community room
2189 — Takes in two grandchildren after her daughter's death; archive work slows considerably

physical_description.heritage: Ubiquitous Diaspora blend: 34.2% Sub-Saharan African, 24.1% East Asian, 19.2% South Asian, 15.9% Southeast Asian, 6.6% Hispanic/Latin American. This creates a rich, warm deep brown complexion with golden undertones, broad facial structure reflecting multiple continents, and the genetic diversity characteristic of the 2226 Great Lakes Metropolitan Zone.
physical_description.build: Compact and lean, spine gently kyphotic from decades of desk work and age — describes herself as 'folded like good paper.' Wiry strength in her shoulders and hands despite her curve.
physical_description.hair_color: Silver-gray with bioluminescent fiber optic filaments woven through, creating soft cyan-white light in low environments
physical_description.hair_style: Worn loose and shoulder-length, often pinned back with a repurposed data-chip clip or piece of scrap polymer to keep it from her reading lenses
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown, occluded by augmented reading lenses with faint amber Axiom archival overlay interface visible on the lens surface
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm deep brown with golden undertones — the result of Sub-Saharan African, East Asian, South Asian, Southeast Asian, and Hispanic/Latin American ancestry blended together. Sun-weathered but well-maintained, showing the natural variation of mixed-heritage skin.
physical_description.complexion: Full-featured face reflecting four continents: slightly broader nose with West African heritage, defined cheekbones with East and South Asian character, warm brown complexion with subtle golden undertones from the layered ancestry. Fine creases around eyes and mouth from decades of close document work and frequent smiling. Hands show faint pigment stains — blues, reds, graphite — from grandchildren's art projects. Fingernails kept short and practical. No makeup; minimal grooming beyond function.
distinguishing_marks: Faint white scar across the knuckle of her left index finger — a paper cut from an archival document from 2198, never quite healed completely
Small burn mark on her right forearm near the wrist — from a heat-lamination tool accident in her fifties, shaped like a tiny crescent
Bioluminescent filaments throughout her hair create an unusual visual signature, most visible at dusk in Tier 5 environments
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Augmented reading lenses with visible amber-tinted Axiom archival interface; bioluminescent hair filaments that glow softly in dim light. Lower back skeletal reinforcement is subcutaneous and invisible. No external chrome or obvious prosthetics.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves slowly and deliberately, as if remembering the geography of her spine with each step. Sits with hands folded. When speaking about records or stories, her hands animate — quick, precise gestures. She turns her whole torso rather than just her head due to spine curvature. Her gait favors her left leg slightly.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4-5 practical: hand-knitted cardigans in muted colors (charcoal, rust, deep indigo) over simple linen shirts, often with reading glasses on a cord. Loose trousers in neutral fabric, worn smooth at the knees and hems from repeated sitting and kneeling to access low archive shelves. Comfortable slip-on shoes with memory-foam insoles. A weathered canvas satchel she's owned for twenty years, reinforced with duct tape at the corners, always slung across her body — carries paper records, a tablet with the old Axiom interface, and whatever the grandchildren have left in there. No jewelry except a thin band on her left ring finger — a data-band from Zheng-Dao's 2195 service recognition program, worn past its original purpose.
